explanation: An AC voltage on the primary coil (Np turns) drives a changing flux around a shared iron core, and that same flux links every turn of the secondary coil (Ns turns). Because each turn sees the same dPhi/dt, the voltages scale with the turn counts: Vs/Vp = Ns/Np. More secondary turns than primary steps the voltage UP (ratio > 1); fewer steps it DOWN. An ideal transformer conserves power, so the current trades off inversely with the voltage.
bullets: Vs/Vp = Ns/Np: the same core flux links both coils, so voltage follows the turns.
Ns > Np steps up; Ns < Np steps down; Ns = Np is 1:1 isolation.
Transformers only work on AC (changing flux); ideally Vp*Ip = Vs*Is, so power is conserved.
